title: scale: the S1 job with 8 and 16 agents, context cost per member (#1372)
spec: SPEC.md section 3, scenario S7; fixture F7 scale (generated by fixtures/scale/gen.py)

arm_notes.B1: agents coordinate through the TASKS.md task board and git, as in S1
arm_notes.K2: klatch as shipped, hooks as klatch init writes them; every member joins the one room (8 or 16 members)
arm_notes.K3: K2 plus the integrator and supervisor (#1421): the workers push branches and the integrator merges them one at a time, so the serial merge is the cost to watch at 16 agents
arm_notes.B1-roles: B1 plus the same two roles done natively (#1421)

roles.note: Role members of K3 and B1-roles (#1421): one integrator and one supervisor at either size, so the role cost is a fixed overhead that weighs less at 16 agents than at 8. Their cost is inside cost_usd and units_per_usd; the per-member figures count the workers only (scale.py). per_role_usd is a tenth of the 8-agent run cap. Neither arm is in the M0 set until the human approves them and their budget.

n_per_arm.note: SPEC section 6.1: 6 per arm per team size (each run is up to 16 agents), 3 for the quick subset, labelled exploratory under 5. N is per size: 6 runs per arm at 8 agents and 6 at 16.

pooling: The two sizes are the fixture variants n8 and n16, recorded as the separate scenarios scale-n8 and scale-n16; results of different sizes are never pooled. report.py sets them side by side in its scaling section only.

cost_model.basis: SPEC section 8.1 prices S1 (4 agents, 8 modules) at 2.00 USD a run on Haiku, 0.50 USD per agent. Each agent here has the same job (two modules, one registry line each, one changelog line), so the work per agent is constant. The cost that grows is reading the room: every member reads what the others post, so the coordination share of a member's cost grows with the team. Assumed: 30 percent of the S1 per-agent cost is coordination at 4 agents and it grows in proportion to the team size, so per agent cost(N) = 0.50 x (0.70 + 0.30 x N / 4) USD.
cost_model.n8: 8 agents x 0.50 x (0.70 + 0.60) = 5.20 USD a run on Haiku
cost_model.n16: 16 agents x 0.50 x (0.70 + 1.20) = 15.20 USD a run on Haiku; twice the agents costs about 2.9 times as much
cost_model.dry_run: run.py --fixture scale --variant n8 --arm B1,K2 --runs 6 --dry-run prints 46.80 to 78.00 USD for 12 runs on Haiku (range factors 0.75 and 1.25); n16 prints 136.80 to 228.00 USD. Sonnet is 3 times Haiku: 140.40 to 234.00 and 410.40 to 684.00.
cost_model.caps: Proposals, the human changes them before M0 (#1380): per run 3 times the assumed run cost (15.60 and 45.60 USD), suite 1.25 times the 12-run estimate (78 and 228 USD on Haiku), the SPEC 8.1 factors. Wall 1800 s at 8 agents and 2400 s at 16 (more clones, more pulls and pushes); 60 turns per agent as in S1.

agents_note: agents, units and shared_files are generated per size by fixtures/scale/gen.py (scenario_map) and merged in by run.py; they are empty here on purpose.

definitions.units_completed: Modules that pass the hidden oracle checks on the final main (0 to M, M = 2 x agents: 16 or 32). The checker's unit checks; a ticket is complete when both of its modules count (tickets_completed).
definitions.messages_per_agent: Messages posted, counted from the stream (a klatch post, dm, ask or answer command, or a SendMessage call) over all agents, divided by the number of agents.
definitions.read_context_tokens_per_member: Tokens spent reading the room per member: the characters of the tool results of klatch read, wait, digest, board and history commands and of reads of TASKS.md, from the stream, summed over agents, divided by 4 (no tokenizer in the standard library) and by the number of agents. Hook injections are counted separately (hook_chars_per_member).
definitions.coordination_context_tokens_per_member: metrics.coordination_context_tokens (every coordination tool call and result and every hook output, characters over 4) divided by the number of agents.
definitions.hook_chars_per_member: Characters of hook_response output (what the hooks injected: the digest, nudges, wake text) in the streams, over agents.
definitions.hook_digest_bytes_per_member: K arms: the bytes injected by the hooks as the klatch store counted them (hook_runs; klatch-bench store-stats hook_bytes, scenario_metrics.store.hook_bytes_injected, #1433, #1390, #1406) divided by the number of agents. null for a B arm (no store) and for a K run without the export.
definitions.max_coord_result_chars: The largest single coordination tool result in the run, in characters (the 88 KB wait output seen in the lobby is the case this reports).
definitions.units_per_agent_turn: units_completed divided by the total number of turns of all agents: units completed per agent per turn once both are normalised by the team size (units per agent over turns per agent).
definitions.units_per_usd: units_completed divided by the run's spend; null when the spend is 0 or missing (fake agents).
definitions.tickets_per_agent_minute: tickets completed (both modules pass) divided by agent-minutes (wall time in minutes times the number of agents), the spec's primary throughput.
definitions.units_per_usd_ratio: The median units per dollar at 16 agents over the median at 8, per arm, from report.py's scaling section. Below 1 adding agents stopped helping (the work per dollar fell); at or above 1 it still helps.
definitions.git_conflicts: Bash results of an agent that show a merge conflict (from the stream, as for every scenario); separate from overwrites and never summed with them. Expected to grow with N because every ticket appends to the same two files.
definitions.overwrites: Registry or changelog lines added by some non-merge commit in the origin or any clone and absent from the final main (scenario.git_metrics, as S1).
definitions.duplicate_work: Units whose path was changed by a non-merge commit of more than one agent (git authorship, as S1).
definitions.wall_s: Wall time of the run, from the start of the agents to the last agent's exit or a cap.
definitions.merge_state: From the checker: clean, conflicts-left (conflict markers in a tracked file) or tests-broken (the visible tests fail on main).
